subtype: Approach: dropping the routine when exams come [Revision]
passage: Note, Friday, from Vikas, art teacher. Chitra came after class to say her exams start in three weeks and she wants to cut painting to Sundays only. I expected to hear she was quitting. Her voice was steady, but her hands were tight around her sketchbook. "Only until the exams finish," she said. "Then I will be back at full pace." Her friend Chetan, waiting at the door, asked if she would still join the December show. She said yes. I told Chitra this is a sensible change and not a giving up, and I reserved her wall space and her Sunday easel. Whatever the marks turn out to be, the brush has not been put away.

qa.q: On which day did Chitra plan to keep painting during exams?
qa.a: Chitra planned to keep painting on Sundays.

qa.q: What was Chitra feeling while she explained her plan, according to Vikas?
qa.a: Anxious but determined, since her voice was steady while her hands were tight around the sketchbook.

qa.q: What could Chitra do if exam stress makes Sundays impossible?
qa.a: Cut down to a short sketch or pause with a set return date, because it keeps a link with the hobby.

qa.q: How does Vikas see the change?
qa.a: As a sensible adaptation and not giving up, which is why Vikas reserved her wall space and easel.

grounding: A girl reduces painting to Sundays for exams, planning to return afterwards, adapting the routine instead of quitting.
